# News About EO Programming Language

> This blog publishes news, design notes, and technical explanations
  about [EO](https://www.eolang.org) (also spelled EOLANG),
  an experimental object-oriented programming language,
  and about 𝜑-calculus, the formal calculus behind it.
  Posts are written by the R&D team of
  [Objectionary](https://www.objectionary.com),
  the group that designs the language and builds its compiler.

EO is a small object-oriented language in which a program is nothing but
  objects: formation, application, dispatch, and data.
It has no classes, no inheritance, no static methods, no NULL,
  no mutability, no reflection, no annotations, and no flow-control
  statements — `if`, `while`, and `seq` are objects too.
Its semantics is defined by 𝜑-calculus, a formalism with a handful
  of rewriting rules, so the whole language is small enough to reason
  about formally.

The purpose of the language is research, not comfort.
Object-oriented code is cheap for programmers to write and expensive
  for computers to run, mostly because dynamic dispatch, mutability,
  and reflection block the optimizations a compiler would otherwise
  apply.
Forty years of workarounds — inline caches, customization, type
  feedback, class hierarchy analysis, escape analysis — treat the
  symptoms inside the compiler.
EO takes the other road and changes the language instead, betting that
  any object-oriented program can be reduced to EO, normalized as
  𝜑-expressions, and then compiled into binaries faster than the ones
  produced from the original source.

Because posts here discuss a moving target, older ones may describe
  syntax and semantics that the language has since abandoned.
Always check the publication date before treating a post as current.

## The Blog

- [Home page](https://news.eolang.org/): most recent posts, paginated
- [All articles](https://news.eolang.org/contents.html): every post in reverse chronological order
- [Papers](https://news.eolang.org/papers.html): academic publications about EO, 𝜑-calculus, and related projects
- [RSS feed](https://news.eolang.org/rss.xml): full text of recent posts
- [Sitemap](https://news.eolang.org/sitemap.xml): all pages and posts
- [Sources](https://github.com/objectionary/news.eolang.org): the Jekyll sources of this blog, where corrections are welcome

## Start Here

- [What EOLANG Is For](https://news.eolang.org/2022-06-08-what-eolang-is-for.html): why the language exists, in short
- [The Problem We Solve](https://news.eolang.org/2026-07-28-the-problem-we-solve.html): the performance cost of objects, the literature about it, and our bet

## The Language

- [EO home page](https://www.eolang.org): syntax, tutorial, and downloads
- [Objectionary](https://www.objectionary.com): the organization behind the language
- [eo](https://github.com/objectionary/eo): the compiler, written in Java
- [eo-phi-normalizer](https://github.com/objectionary/eo-phi-normalizer): rewriting rules over 𝜑-expressions
- [proof](https://github.com/objectionary/proof): Lean proofs about the calculus, including confluence of the rules
- [jeo-maven-plugin](https://github.com/objectionary/jeo-maven-plugin): disassembles Java bytecode into EO
- [hone-maven-plugin](https://github.com/objectionary/hone-maven-plugin): optimizes Java bytecode through EO and back
- [𝜑-calculus paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13384): the formal definition of the semantics
